chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: Florida stay and the integrated Sir John hotel
summary: He went back to New York for court dates while his belongings stayed in Florida; they lived at an integrated hotel.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You stayed in Florida how long?
And then you would go back to New York?

Then I went back to New York on one of my court dates, and my attorney asked for a continuance, and the Judge, he was an Englishman. I forget his name. He said, "No, this case has been on the docket long enough. We'll dispose of it today." I said, "Oh-oh." All of my belongings are in Florida, you know. And it just happened that my youngest daughter -- now, I was going with her mother, she made a trip from here to New York, in case I had to go to jail, to bring all of my things out here to my mother. In the meanwhile, she got her a job at FAO Schwartz Toy Company there on Fifth Avenue, the biggest toy company in the world. Just to be doing something while she was there, you know. And I went to Florida and she joined me in Florida. And we were in this integrated hotel, the Lord Calvert. They later named it the St. John or something like that.
The Sir John, yeah. Well, we were there for the opening of it, and it was integrated, you know. They had their own security guard.

Yes. A pretty place. The police wasn't called in there at all. It was out of bounds for the police, you know. So we had a swimming pool there, nice accomodations, like you could enter from the street into your apartment, or you could enter from the inside, by the swimming pool, into your apartment, you know. Apartment. What am I saying? It's one room and cooking facilities and a bathroom, a single.
But it was an attractive, well kept place.
Billy Strayhorn showed me pictures of it.
